settings.title: The rulebook
settings.body: Most leagues won't let you play in pierced jewelry. Tape over it, take it out, or sit out. A magnetic stud comes off in a second when a ref asks, and goes straight back in after the whistle.

settings.title: The healing
settings.body: A fresh piercing wants weeks of downtime and no contact, and it can reject or get infected if you sweat into it. Nobody is giving up a season for an earring. There is nothing to heal here because there is no hole.

settings.title: The one you lose
settings.body: Backs work loose. Helmets and headgear rip them out. You find one stud in the gym bag and never the other. Every kit ships with three, so losing one is an inconvenience instead of a write-off.

settings.heading: Piercings and sports don't mix.
settings.intro: Every athlete who has wanted a stud has run into the same three walls.
settings.closer: So we built one that doesn't need a hole.

settings.name: Clean

settings.image_alt: Man in sunglasses wearing a mid-size stud
settings.name: Standard
settings.text: The one most guys land on. Visible from across the court, not from space.

settings.image_alt: Man in water wearing a large stud and chain
settings.name: Loud
settings.text: You want people to notice. They will.

settings.heading: Find your fit in 10 seconds.
settings.intro: Every kit ships with all three sizes. Put each one on, look in the mirror, keep the one that looks like it was made for your face. No measuring, no guessing, no exchange.

settings.title: Easy on
settings.body: Front on the lobe, magnet behind it. It pulls itself into place. Two seconds, one hand, no mirror, no help from anyone.

settings.title: Stays on
settings.body: It will not shake loose, sweat off, or get dragged out by a jersey coming over your head. It holds through contact and sits flat enough for headgear to go over it.

settings.title: Off when you say so
settings.body: Pinch and pull. Coming off takes a deliberate move with two fingers, which is exactly what you want when a ref asks you to take it out before tip-off.

settings.image_alt: Man wearing a stud in the barber chair
settings.heading: To be the best you need to feel like it.
settings.intro: Confidence is not a small thing. It is also useless if you spend the whole game checking your ear.
